Moneys in the fund are appropriated 6 to the department of veterans affairs (IDVA) to be used to 7 incentivize counties to effectively increase veteran outreach 8 and efficiency in the application for individual federal 9 veteran compensation. 10 Under current law, IDVA annually allocates $10,000 from the 11 fund to each county commission of veteran affairs (CCVA) or to 12 each county sharing the services of an executive director or 13 administrator, and each county must report on the expenditure 14 of its allocation in a form agreed to by IDVA and the county 15 representatives. The bill strikes the specified allocation 16 amount. The bill provides that for FY 2026-2027, each county 17 shall receive an equal amount of moneys from the fund. For 18 subsequent fiscal years, allocations shall be based on 19 performance criteria established by IDVA. 20 The bill requires the veterans services excellence training 21 program and administration account to fund training and support 22 for CCVAs and strikes provisions that credit remaining moneys 23 in the fund to the account and that allocate $3,000 to each 24 CCVA or each county sharing the services of an executive 25 director or administrator for training expenses. 26 The bill requires IDVA to verify that each executive 27 director and administrator of a CCVA be in compliance with 28 education and training standards established by the commandant 29 and removes the requirement to verify they are proficient in 30 general computer use. 31 The bill requires IDVA to create a statewide standardized 32 electronic claim system through which county veterans service 33 offices must submit all United States department of veterans 34 affairs claims and requires IDVA to communicate county veterans 35 -6- LSB 5189XL (5) 91 sc/ns 6/ 7 S.F. _____ H.F. _____ service office performance metrics to CCVAs and boards of 1 supervisors.
